eligibility.evidence: Sonnet 4.5 is administered the blicket detector causal-learning task (Gopnik & Sobel 2000; Kosoy et al. 2022a cited, Sections 1 and 4). A plain base agent is tested beside two scaffolded agents. Accuracy is new behaviour (Tables 5-6). Borderline because the paper is an architecture study and the agent acts through environment actions.

A.title: Separable Pathways for Causal Reasoning: How Architectural Scaffolding Enables Hypothesis-Space Restructuring in LLM Agents

paradigms.name: Extended blicket detector (conjunctive/disjunctive baselines; hidden moderator, order-sensitive, stochastic conditions)

effects.label: NO-HUMAN-REFERENCE
effects.location: Table 5a, Section 5.3 and Table 6 (hidden moderator, reasoning-eligible accuracy, Base agent); ceiling on standard conditions, Panel 1; order-sensitive and stochastic, Table 4. Reported by agent and condition, not pooled.

E.headline: Context graphs raise reasoning-eligible accuracy after a hidden rule change; dynamic behaviours reduce premature submission; no gain for order-sensitive or stochastic rules.

G.notes: Single model family; no human data; the dependent measure is the architecture contrast, not Sonnet versus humans. Preregistration is mentioned for Runs 04 and 06 but not cited. Code is promised on acceptance, yet the Limitations say it is released. Reasoning-eligible accuracy was defined post hoc (Section 4.3.2). Many iterative runs.
